question: Which of the following is the autobiography of the first Indian President Dr. Rajendra Prasad?
solution:
The Correct Answer is **Atmakatha**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rajendra Prasad, **who would later become the** first President of India**, penned his autobiography titled **"Atmakatha" **during his **three-year imprisonment **in **Bankipur Jail.**
 
• Following the Indian Independence Movement, he joined the** Indian National Congress **and played a significant role in the freedom struggle.
 
• Prasad actively participated in key events such as the** 'Salt Satyagraha' of 1931 **and the **'Quit India Movement' of 1942**.
 
• His contributions extended to the drafting of the Indian Constitution, a monumental task in the nation's history.
 
• In 1950, he was unanimously elected as the inaugural President of the Republic of India by the Constituent Assembly, a position he held until 1962. 
 
• Rajendra Prasad's remarkable service to the nation earned him the prestigious **Bharat Ratna,** **India's highest civilian award, in 1962**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **"Atmavrittanta"** holds significant historical value as it offers insights into the life in 19th-century Gujarat, encompassing aspects of religion, society, economy, ethics, and education prevalent during that era.
 
• **"A Shot at History"** presents a narrative by Bindra, emphasizing the importance of personal drive and determination over external factors like training and coaching in achieving one's goals. Bindra recounts his journey to becoming a professional shooter, crediting various coaches who contributed to his success.
 
• **"My Country My Life"** is an autobiographical work by L. K. Advani, a prominent Indian politician who served as Deputy Prime Minister from 2002 to 2004 and held the position of Leader of the Opposition in the 15th Lok Sabha. Released on March 19, 2008, the book was launched by Abdul Kalam, the former President of India.
